source.title: Sobolev norm inconsistency of kernel interpolation

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies consistency of kernel minimum-norm interpolation, but does not test a double-descent curve or rely on that finding. Its discussion of neural-network generalization is background and citations.
record.gate_note: The paper cites work on neural networks interpolating noisy data, but reports no neural-network results. Its own theorem bounds generalization error for kernel interpolation as sample size grows; it does not compare test error across model sizes, training epochs, or sample counts near an interpolation threshold. The theorem is recorded as a related finding under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: A purely theoretical paper. It lower-bounds the error of kernel minimum-norm interpolation, in [H]^γ norms, as sample size n grows at fixed input dimension. The estimator interpolates at every n. There is no sweep of capacity, epochs or samples across an interpolation threshold, and no test-error curve. Belkin et al. 2019 is cited only as background on benign overfitting. The result bears on whether interpolating kernels generalize, not on the double-descent shape.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also say the result is evidence that tuning the ridge parameter is necessary for minimax-optimal rates. They say it recovers and generalizes Li et al. 2024 without that paper's Hölder-continuity assumption. They note it applies to the neural tangent kernel of shallow ReLU networks under lazy training, but not beyond lazy training.
record.recipe_differences: No double-descent method or curve is tested.
record.method_sensitivity: The stated consistency result depends on the smoothness index γ, embedding index α*, eigenvalue-decay parameters β and ζ, and whether Mα* is finite.

fits_no_version.finding: In fixed input dimension, kernel minimum-norm interpolation is inconsistent in [H]^γ norm when γ > 3(α* − 1/β), and generalizes poorly at equality. Tuned kernel ridge regression is minimax optimal in the same norms.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In low fixed dimension, interpolating (ridgeless) kernel regression does not generalize, even in norms slightly stronger than L2. Benign interpolation needs high dimension, and tuning the regularization is necessary for optimal rates.

record.problems: No empirical model-size, epoch, or near-threshold sample-size comparisons are reported; the findings are theoretical and conditional on stated assumptions.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep; no neural networks.
Sample size varies only within the always-interpolating regime; no threshold or non-monotonicity result.
No capacity axis or risk curve past an interpolation point.
Effective dimension is defined as a tool, not as a predictor of peak location.
Shows ridgeless interpolation is inconsistent while tuned ridge is minimax optimal. No peak, noise sweep or multiple-descent analysis.

record.verdict_notes: Record's relation, tranche and empty labels are confirmed. The paper sits in the benign-overfitting literature that is adjacent to V4 and V6, but it measures no double-descent curve.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep or test-error curve around a training-set interpolation threshold.
No comparison of test error at different sample counts near an interpolation threshold.
No capacity sweep or risk curve across model classes.
No unified effective-complexity measure is evaluated as a predictor of peak location.
No peak analysis involving label noise, multiple descent, or optimally tuned regularization.
No comparison of descent curves under alternative complexity counts.

rows.subject: kernel minimum-norm interpolation (1.2)
rows.operation_detail: Derives a lower bound on generalization error as sample size n grows under the theorem's assumptions.

conditions.value: bounded measurable kernel; noise condition 3.1; eigenvalue decay 3.5; fP* ∈ [H]γν; fixed input dimension

rows.measure: Conditional expected squared generalization error in [H]γν norm, E[||[f̂n]ν − fP*||²γ | X]
rows.value: The error tends to ∞ as n → ∞, with probability at least 1 − δ.
rows.uncertainty: Probability guarantee: at least 1 − δ for any δ ∈ (0, 1).
rows.note: A consistency result for kernel interpolation in a specified function norm; it does not establish the shape of test error versus model size, epochs, or sample count near an interpolation threshold.
rows.check: Row is correctly unlinked. The value is an asymptotic theorem: error diverges as n grows, always at interpolation. It is not a measured test-error curve versus capacity, epochs or samples near a threshold, and has no baseline. It could loosely touch V4, since an interpolating kernel fails to generalize in fixed dimension, but V4 concerns risk improving as capacity grows past interpolation. No capacity axis exists here.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
